Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address Property Maintenance and Rehabilitation Appeals Board
on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum
described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address the Board, please complete
the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the Secretary. Property
Maintenance and Rehabilitation Appeals Board will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during
discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. Property Maintenance and Rehabilitation Appeals Board will hear
public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or
unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The Board may direct staff to investigate and/or
schedule certain matters for consideration at a future Property Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation Appeals
Board meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Board:
  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the Board as a whole and not directed to individual Property
  Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation Appeals Board members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a
City meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the Secretary’s office, (562) 929-5744.
Assisted listening devices are available at this meeting. Ask the Secretary if you desire to use this device. Upon
request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative
formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services
are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide
accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Board regarding any item on this agenda after
it has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the Community Development Department, City Hall,
12700 Norwalk Boulevard during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday to Thursday and 8:00
a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5744. You may also contact the City Clerk via email at
recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  BUILDING REHABILITATION APPEALS BOARD
  SPECIAL MEETING
  JUNE 13, 2018

The meeting was called to order by Chair Juan at 7:07 p.m. in the Norwalk City Hall,
Council Chambers, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Present were Board
Member Apodaca, Vice Chair Barragan, and Chair Juan. Board Members Lopez and
Collins were absent. Also present were Bing H. Hyun, Acting Director of Community
Development; Anthony Weimholt, Building and Safety Manager; Norma Sifuentes, Code
Compliance Inspector; Adriana Figueroa, Administrative Services Manager; and Ruth
Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

REORGANIZATION OF THE BOARD
The Board, by unanimous voice vote, appointed Kim Apodaca to serve as Chair for the
upcoming year and Rosa Barragan to serve as Vice Chair.

MEETING MINUTES
The Board approved the minutes of the Special Meetings of June 14, 2017 and May 23,
2018.

DELINQUENT TRASH AND REFUSE COLLECTION ACCOUNTS
Report on delinquent trash accounts and the hearing of any objections of the
property owners liable for unpaid trash and refuse services in accordance with
the provisions of Chapter 8.48 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.

Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Adriana Figueroa,
Administrative Services Manager, presented a report stating that a combined total of
1,948 notices were mailed by CR&R and Republic Services by May 3, 2018; that the
delinquent accounts totaled $489,103.07 at the time the notices were mailed; that
CR&R mailed 214 notices in the amount of $50,961.64 and Republic Services mailed
1,734 notices in the amount of $438,141.43; that Republic Services included an
additional quarter in the billing amount, which accounts for the significant increase
from previous years in the total amount; that this issue has since been corrected; that
a City administrative fee of $25 was added to each delinquent account, and is
included in the amounts shown; that staff recommends that the Board forward the
listed properties to the City Council with a recommendation that the delinquent
properties be placed on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding balance is paid
prior to July 31, 2018.

Ms. Figueroa further stated that representatives from both companies are here to
answer any questions that the Board may have.
 Minutes of the Special Meeting

Since there were no persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Apodaca closed the
public hearing.

Board Member Juan indicated that he can make the findings as recommended by
staff.

It was moved by Board Member Juan and seconded by Chair Apodaca to direct staff
to forward the listed properties to the City Council with a recommendation that the
delinquent properties be placed on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding
balance is paid prior to July 31, 2018.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Board Member Juan, Vice Chair Barragan, and Chair Apodaca
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Board Member Collins and Board Member Lopez.

DELINQUENT WEEDS AND LITTER COLLECTION FEES
Report on the cost of abatement of weeds and litter and the hearing of any
objections of property owners liable to be assessed for such abatement in
accordance with the provisions of Chapter 8.28 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.

Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Anthony Weimholt, Building
and Safety Manager, presented a report commenting on the list of properties that were
invoiced for weed and litter abatement performed pursuant to Chapter 8.28 of the
Norwalk Municipal Code for which reimbursement has not been received; and he stated
that the outstanding charges amount to $21,081.29. He further stated that Item No. 6
on the list makes reference to 10823 and 10829 Hopland Street; that prior to this
meeting, the list was corrected and a copy was given to the Board members, indicating
that the lot is an unimproved vacant parcel on Hopland Street; and that it is staff’s
recommendation that the Board forward the listed properties to the City Council with a
recommendation that the delinquent amounts be placed as a lien on the County Tax
Roll unless the outstanding balance is paid prior to August 1, 2018.

Syed M. Kaleem, the property owner of the vacant parcel on Hopland Street,
addressed the Board. He commented on his court case stating that he received a
notice today from the Superior Court that all charges have been reversed.

Building and Safety Manager Weimholt stated that the City filed a criminal complaint
against Mr. Kaleem for continuous violations of the Municipal Code; that the court case

was heard by a judge; however, due to Mr. Kaleem not being properly advised of his
rights, the Appellate Court reversed the judge’s action and declared the case null and
void; that this case is completely separate from the weed and litter invoice; and that the
City performs weed and litter abatement when an owner does not take responsibility.

Mr. Kaleem stated that he has been maintaining the property himself.

Chair Apodaca stated that the report indicates that the City did perform weed and litter
abatement on September 7, 2017; and that the invoice in the amount of $1,113.55 for
that work was sent to Mr. Kaleem.

Acting Director Hyun stated that, for the record, he would ask the Building Official to
explain what happened on the property.

Building and Safety Manager Weimholt indicated that on September 7, 2017, the City’s
vendor removed overgrown weeds and trash from the property as well as a pigeon
coop from the rear of the property; and that on October 16, 2017 the invoice in the
amount of $1,113.55 for that work was mailed to the address given by Mr. Kaleem.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Apodaca closed
the public hearing.

It was moved by Vice Chair Barragan and seconded by Board Member Juan to direct
staff to forward the listed properties to the City Council with a recommendation that the
delinquent amounts be placed as a lien on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding
balance is paid prior to August 1, 2018.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Board Member Juan, Vice Chair Barragan, and Chair Apodaca
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Board Member Collins and Board Member Lopez.

SUBJECT: DELINQUENT WEEDS AND LITTER COLLECTION FEES
  Report on the cost of abatement of weeds and litter and the hearing
  of any objections of property owners liable to be assessed for such
  abatement in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 8.28 of the
  Norwalk Municipal Code.

BACKGROUND:

Chapter 8.28 of the Norwalk Municipal Code requires that the owner or person having
control of any private property maintain the premises free of weeds, litter and noxious or
rank growth. If the property is found to be in violation of this Chapter, the property is
posted for weed and litter removal as required by the Norwalk Municipal Code.

The Norwalk Municipal Code allows the owner or person having control of said property
to file within five (5) days after proper notice is given, any objection of this abatement
with the City Clerk’s office.

Section 8.28.230 allows a duly appointed City Officer to enter upon any property to
which a public nuisance is found, after notice to abate has been posted as described by
this section and no objections have been filed with the City Clerk’s office.
 Property Maintenance and  Page No. 2
Building Rehabilitation Appeals Board  June 12, 2019

A “Declaration of Substandard” is filed with the Los Angeles County Recorder’s Office
prior to all weed & litter nuisance abatement to notify interested parties of the pending
cost associated with the abatement.

Section 8.28.240 requires that the City Officer keep an account of the abatement
expenses and submit an itemized written report to the Property Maintenance and
Building Rehabilitation Appeals Board for confirmation. Property owners liable to be
assessed may bring objections to such assessments before the Board.

The Property Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation Appeals Board, after hearing
such objections, must report to the City Council with its recommendation as to the
disposition of the assessment. The City Council may modify the report if it is deemed
necessary and confirm the report by motion or resolution. The cost of abatement
constitutes a special assessment.

After the assessment is confirmed by City Council, it is forwarded to the County
Assessor as a lien on the lot or parcel.

Attached is a list of properties that were invoiced for weed and litter abatement
performed pursuant to Chapter 8.28 of the Norwalk Municipal Code for which
reimbursement has not been received. The total outstanding charges amount to
$1,298.45.

RECOMMENDATION:

That the Board direct staff to forward the listed properties to the City Council with a
recommendation that the delinquent amounts be placed as a lien on the County Tax
Roll unless the outstanding balance is paid prior to August 1, 2019.

SUBJECT:  EMERGENCY BOARD-UP COSTS
  Report on the cost of emergency board-ups and the hearing of
  any objections of property owners liable to be assessed for
  such abatement in accordance with the provisions of Chapter
  15.32 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.

BACKGROUND:

Whenever unsafe conditions are found to create a hazard to safety, health or public
welfare, by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, fire hazard, disaster
damage, vandalism or abandonment, staff takes an emergency action to secure or
otherwise abate the hazardous conditions to protect the public. The property owner on
record is sent an invoice of the costs incurred by the City for this process. Unpaid
invoices are processed as a special assessment to the property.

The purpose of the meeting tonight is to provide the opportunity for any interested party
to voice their concerns or objections to such assessments before the Board.

NMC Section 15.32.150A specifies: “all buildings or structures which are structurally
unsafe or not provided with adequate egress, or which constitute a fire hazard, or are
otherwise dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use constitute a
hazard to safety or health or public welfare, by reason of inadequate maintenance,
dilapidation, obsolescence, fire hazard, disaster damage, or abandonment, as specified
 Property Maintenance and  Page No. 2
Building Rehabilitation Appeals Board – Emergency Board-up  June 12, 2019

in this Code or in any other effective ordinance or statute, are, for the purpose of this
section, unsafe buildings and constitute an unsafe condition. All such unsafe buildings
or conditions are hereby declared to be public nuisances and shall be abated by repair,
rehabilitation, improvement, removal, or demolition, in whole or part, in accordance with
the procedures specified in this code.”

NMC Section 15.32.170 specifies: “when any unoccupied building or structure is not
properly secured, locked or closed and is accessible to juveniles, transients and
unauthorized persons and is a health and/or safety hazard to the adjacent community,
and the Building Official so finds, the Building Official shall serve the record owner and
(if not the owner) the person having control of such building or structure with a notice to
secure or close the same forthwith so as to prevent unauthorized persons from gaining
access thereto.”

NMC Section 15.32.170.12 establishes emergency procedures: “whenever in the
opinion of the Building Official the conditions described in Section 15.32.170 constitute
such an immediate hazard that access to the building or structure must be limited or
closed forthwith or within less than the designated period, or either the Sheriff, Public
Safety Director, or Chief of the Fire Department so finds and so notifies the Building
Official, he or she shall limit access to such building after giving such notice to the
record owner or the person in charge, or both as the circumstances will permit or
without any notice whatever when, in the opinion of the Building Official, Sheriff, Public
Safety Director, or the Chief of the Fire Department, immediate action is necessary.”

A “Declaration of Substandard” is filed with the Los Angeles County Recorder’s Office
as part of the nuisance abatement process to notify interested parties of the pending
cost associated with the abatement.

DISCUSSION:

Notice of the abatement expenses are sent as an invoice to the property owners of
record. Staff keeps an accounting of the abatement expenses associated with each
property. Attached is an itemized summary showing the outstanding costs to date.
Property owners were mailed the required 45-day notice of the proposed lien
assessment for these unpaid board up costs, which allows owners to bring objections
over their property assessments before the Board.

The Board shall hear all objections or protests of property owners liable to be assessed
for the delinquent fees, and may make revisions to the report as well as
recommendations to the City Council with regard to disposition of the delinquent fees.

Upon confirmation by the City Council, the cost of abatement will constitute a lien on the
property and may be paid to the Director of Finance prior to August 1, 2019. The
unpaid liens will be delivered to the County Auditor to be collected at the time and in the
manner of other taxes on the property.

Attached is a list of properties that were invoiced for emergency board-up work

performed pursuant to Chapter 15.32 of the Norwalk Municipal Code for which
reimbursement has not been received, in the amount of $33,040.60. Please note that
this list also contains the properties from the 2017-2018 Fiscal Year in the amount of
$9,578.16 which were previously presented to the Board at its meeting on June 13,
2018. Although the Board approved the amount be placed as a lien on the County Tax
Roll at that meeting, the City was unable to take this action due to inadvertently missing
the required 45 day noticing to each property owner.

RECOMMENDATION:

That the Board direct staff to forward the listed properties to the City Council with a
recommendation that the delinquent amounts be placed as a lien on the County Tax
Roll unless the outstanding balance is paid prior to August 1, 2019.
